title: Endurance
definition: Endurance is continuing in faith and obedience under pressure, suffering, delay, opposition, or weariness.
summary: Endurance keeps trusting and obeying Christ when life is hard.
christFocus: Jesus endured the cross and strengthens His people to endure with hope.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Endurance is the Spirit-strengthened ability to remain faithful under pressure. It is not denial of pain; it is continued trust in God while pain is real.

Scripture connects endurance with hope, maturity, and future reward. Trials test faith, but God uses them to strengthen His people.

Jesus is the supreme example and source of endurance. He endured the cross for the joy set before Him, and believers look to Him when weary.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Hardship can make people want to quit, compromise, or believe God has forgotten them. Endurance matters because it teaches believers how to remain faithful when obedience is costly.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look to Jesus when you are tired. Ask for strength for today's obedience, receive support from the Church, and remember that God is producing steadfastness through trial.
